Photograph a ticket

Take a photo Choose images

Or drag photos here, or paste one from the clipboard. Several at once is fine — each photo becomes one ticket.

Reading happens entirely in your browser — no photo ever leaves this device, and no part of this needs the internet. For the best results photograph the ticket square on, in good light, with the whole form in frame.

Waiting to be confirmed

What the reader looks for

Any of these labels on the paper ticket will be picked up, with or without a colon: System no, System name, System id, Business units, Answer code, Priority, Status, Reported by, Issue, Date. Failing a label, it falls back to matching your system names, spotting an id that fits that system's pattern, and finding a four digit code it recognises. Anything it cannot find is flagged rather than guessed.

Reference data

the 22 systems and their codes, the 4 business units, and the answer code list

The systems and their configuration item codes are the ones from the configuration item sheet; systems 15–22 have no code recorded yet, and the app will not invent one — add them here when you have them. The four business units are named as they are on the sheet — 1 to 4 — so give them words here if you would rather read them that way. The answer codes are a starter list; replace them with yours. A code identifies its system, so two systems cannot share one; a ticket whose code differs from the one on record is flagged, never blocked. Changes are saved in this browser — use the Data tab to export them for a colleague.
